title: Optimize quant kernels: INT8/FP8 smoothquant + dequant fusion + kvcache-aware scheduling
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: Reduce inference latency and memory traffic for quantized (INT8/FP8) models by fusing dequantization into GEMM kernels, folding smoothquant scales into the int8 path, and making the scheduler KV-cache aware so it avoids redundant memory copies during continuous batching. This PR implements three coordinated changes: 1) a fused dequant+matmul kernel used when model weights are stored in quantized INT8/FP8 formats and activations require dequantization; 2) smoothquant scale folding into the quantized kernel so per-channel scaling is applied on-the-fly without an explicit dequant pass; 3) kvcache-aware scheduling and batch coalescing that keeps KV pages resident on the same device and batches requests by compatible sequence-length/kv-state to minimize memcpys and kernel launch overhead. The description below summarizes design, benchmarks, and rollout plan. Design summary: - Fused dequant+GEMM: new kernel reorders work so dequantization and column-major GEMM are fused in a single CUDA/ROCm kernel. This reduces global memory traffic and eliminates a separate dequant buffer. The kernel supports both INT8 (symmetric/asymmetric) and FP8 weight layouts. - SmoothQuant folding: when model metadata indicates smoothquant scales are available, scale multiplication is fused into the quantized kernel's per-channel input transform. This avoids separate scale passes and preserves numerical stability by applying scaling with quantization-aware accumulation. - KVCACHE-aware scheduler: scheduler tags requests with KV cache fingerprints and coalesces continuous-batching candidates that share compatible KV memory layouts or that can reuse resident KV pages. When possible, the scheduler pins KV pages per inference worker to avoid host-device roundtrips for repeated prefix decoding. This change also adds a small heuristic to avoid cross-device migration for mixed-precision fallbacks. Benchmarks: - INT8: 18-22% p99 latency reduction across our Lambda-7B baseline (batch sizes 1-8, seq 512), up to 30% throughput increase for steady-state batched workloads. - FP8 fallback path: 10-14% latency reduction relative to previous FP8 implementation due to lower memory movement. - End-to-end quality: measured log-prob differences on evaluation prompts show <0.15% average relative change against the float baseline for the INT8 path with smoothquant folding; we include regression tests to track any drift. Compatibility & rollout: - The kernels are guarded behind runtime feature flags and model metadata checks. By default the old codepath remains active. - We added a canary rollout strategy (10% of traffic -> 50% -> 100%) with automatic rollback if per-model perplexity or token-level error rates exceed configured thresholds. - No public API changes. Implementation notes: - Added new unified kernel files (cuda/quant_fused_gemm.cu and rocm/quant_fused_gemm.hip) with an internal registration mechanism to select the kernel based on weight dtype/format. - Updated the execution planner to annotate requests with kv-cache fingerprints and sequence length buckets used by continuous batching. - Extended model metadata to include smoothquant scale tensors and quantization layout hints. Checklist: - [x] Kernel implementation and unit tests - [x] Microbenchmarks and integration perf harness runs - [x] Regression tests against float baseline - [x] Canary rollout config and telemetry hooks - [x] Documentation notes for model onboarding and metadata flags Related: ENG-8421 (kernel perf), ENG-8490 (scheduler improvements).
